speaker: Unknown
en: One of the big questions on people's minds these days, is AI doing bad things?
zh: 如今人们心中的一个大问题是，AI 是不是在干坏事？

en: As someone that watches these models think and operate, why is it so hard to catch it thinking badly trying to deceive us?
zh: 作为观察这些模型思考和运作的人，为什么很难抓住它想坏心思、试图欺骗我们？

speaker: Unknown
en: We trained Claude to be helpful, harmless, and honest.
zh: 我们训练 Claude 要乐于助人、无害且诚实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it the case that it's behaving well, but if you look inside actually it's like, oh, I'm only behaving well because Lenny's watching right now.
zh: 是不是存在这种情况：它表现良好，但如果你往内部看，其实是「哦，我表现良好只是因为 Lenny 正在看着」。

speaker: Unknown
en: People's full-time jobs is studying the model, how it thinks, how it operates.
zh: 人们的全职工作就是研究这个模型，它如何思考、如何运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: How long has this been a skillset and a job?
zh: 这成为一项技能和一份工作有多久了？

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most important things to realize if you use language models or think about them is just this very bizarre fact that to make them is not to understand them.
zh: 如果你使用语言模型或思考语言模型，要意识到的最重要的事情之一，就是这个非常离奇的事实：制造它们并不等于理解它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these models do is just a lot of mathematical operations on many numbers.
zh: 这些模型所做的，只是对一大堆数字进行大量的数学运算。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at it, it makes no sense.
zh: 如果你去看它，它毫无意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just have a list of a hundred numbers, the model's doing math, and then you just try to see if there's patterns.
zh: 你只有一个一百个数字的列表，模型在做数学运算，然后你只是试图看看有没有模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are figuring it out the same way we figure out how the brain works, looking for patterns.
zh: 你在弄明白它的方式，和我们弄明白大脑如何工作的方式一样，就是寻找模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You show this image, this part of the brain lights up and you're doing the exact same thing with AI.
zh: 你给大脑看这张图，大脑的这部分就亮起来，而你对 AI 做的是完全一样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, this is so fascinating.
zh: 哇，这太迷人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was this model we were training, it would go crazy.
zh: 我们当时在训练的一个模型，它会疯掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would do some math, it would get to an answer, I think it was 12.
zh: 它会做一些数学运算，得到一个答案，我记得是 12。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would immediately go back and say like, "Oh no, oh my God, the answer actually is for sure 36."
zh: 它会立刻回过头说：「哦不，天哪，答案其实肯定是 36。」

speaker: Unknown
en: It would do math again, it would get to 12.
zh: 它会再做一次数学运算，又得到 12。

speaker: Unknown
en: Slowly it would start descending into madness, writing in all caps, literally saying, "I'm possessed by a demon."
zh: 慢慢地它开始陷入疯狂，用全大写字母书写，甚至说「我被恶魔附身了」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans, if you really boil it down, we're basically next token predictors ourselves.
zh: 人类，如果你真正归根结底，我们基本上自己就是下一个 token 预测器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just trying to figure out the next thing to say.
zh: 我们只是在试图弄清楚接下来要说什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dario is always out there, "This is really dangerous.
zh: Dario 总是在外面说：「这真的很危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got to be really careful."
zh: 我们必须非常小心。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And everyone's just like, "No, he's just saying that for marketing reasons."
zh: 而所有人都在说：「不，他这么说只是为了营销。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it's like, wait, shit, it's really dangerous.
zh: 而现在就像是，等等，糟糕，它真的很危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take the idea that this technology is going to keep improving seriously.
zh: 认真对待这个技术会持续改进的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think about consciousness as a part of this?
zh: 你认为意识是其中的一部分吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just do you think AI is conscious?
zh: 就是说，你认为 AI 有意识吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 哦，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Emmanuel, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Emmanuel，非常感谢你来到这里，欢迎来到这个播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me, Lenny.
zh: 谢谢你的邀请，Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you work on interpretability at Anthropic.
zh: 那么你在 Anthropic 做可解释性工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Explain what that is.

speaker: Unknown
en: Explain what it is you do.
zh: 解释一下你做的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I work in a team of interpretability researchers and our goal is to understand how LLMs like Claude work by looking inside them.
zh: 我在一个可解释性研究员团队工作，我们的目标是通过深入内部观察来理解像 Claude 这样的 LLM 是如何工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most important things to realize if you use language models or think about them is just this very bizarre fact that to make them is not to understand them.
zh: 如果你使用语言模型或思考语言模型，要意识到的最重要的事情之一，就是这个非常离奇的事实：制造它们并不等于理解它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You make them by building this architecture, which is kind of like a scaffold, and then you pass a bunch of data through them and they grow in inscrutable ways.
zh: 你通过构建这种架构来制造它们，它有点像一个脚手架，然后你把大量数据传过它们，它们以难以理解的方式成长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why it's even a thing that we could be wanting to do to study how these models work.
zh: 所以这就是为什么「研究这些模型如何工作」甚至会成为我们想做的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of our research has been on, well, when the models are about to produce one more word, there's actually a whole universe of stuff that happens and we try to untangle as much of it as we can.
zh: 我们的很多研究都集中在：当模型即将产出下一个词时，实际上有整个宇宙的事情在发生，我们试图尽可能多地解开其中的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be a lot of mind-expanding, I don't know, elements to this conversation I expect.
zh: 我预计这次对话会有很多让人大开眼界的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is along these lines, this point that you make that models are not built, they're grown.
zh: 其中一个就是沿着这个方向，你提出的这个观点：模型不是被建造出来的，而是被生长出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speak more to that.
zh: 多讲讲这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: At a really high level, the way a model like Claude works is you train it in these successive phases, like the first phase, which people refer to as pre-training is you just take a large corpus of data, and over this corpus of data, you feed the model as input, the let's say first half of a certain document, and you ask it to predict the word that comes next.
zh: 在非常高的层面上，像 Claude 这样的模型的工作方式是，你在这些相继的阶段中训练它，比如第一个阶段，人们称之为预训练，就是你拿一个大型数据语料库，在这个语料库上，你把比如说某个文档的前半部分作为输入喂给模型，然后要求它预测接下来出现的词。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you do that again and again and again and again for an ungodly amount of data.
zh: 然后你一次又一次又一次地这样做，处理数量极其庞大的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after you do that, there's then this other phase where then you have this fine-tuning phase where maybe instead of arbitrary data, you have a corpus of examples of how the model should behave and that's what you train it on.
zh: 在你做完这些之后，还有另一个阶段，也就是微调阶段，在那里可能不是任意数据，而是有一批关于模型应该如何表现的示例语料库，你就用它来训练模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have examples of dialogue of helpful assistant telling you your favorite recipe or solving coding problems.
zh: 所以你会有一些对话示例，比如乐于助人的助手告诉你你最喜欢的食谱，或者解决编程问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's further details here that I'm just going to skip for a second.
zh: 然后还有一些更细节的内容，我先暂时跳过。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then, okay, so what does that mean that you're doing this process?
zh: 但是，好，那么你在做这个过程意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is this thing that you're training?
zh: 你训练的这个东西是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: All models are, is they take this input, which is a bunch of words, they turn these words into numbers, and then they do some math on these numbers and they get some intermediate results and then they do more math and they get some intermediate results and they do this again and again and again and again many times.
zh: 所有模型所做的，就是接收这个输入，也就是一堆词，把这些词转成数字，然后对这些数字做一些数学运算，得到一些中间结果，然后再做更多数学运算，再得到一些中间结果，然后一次又一次又一次地重复这个过程很多次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at the end they have a final result which then convert back into a word.
zh: 然后在最后，它们会有一个最终结果，这个结果再被转换回一个词。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the math that they do, these computations, that's the part that's grown.
zh: 所以它们做的数学、这些计算，才是增长的那部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the part where it's just like through learning to do this task better, we serve update parameters in one direction or another and then they learn some formulas.
zh: 那就是通过学习更好地完成这个任务，我们以某个方向或另一个方向更新参数，然后它们学到了一些公式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have no idea what they are.
zh: 我们完全不知道这些公式是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the goal of my team is to study both what these formulas mean in the end and also what these intermediate results are.
zh: 而我团队的目标就是既研究这些公式最终意味着什么，也研究这些中间结果是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we decode them and can we see what the model is doing as it's doing all of this intermediate stuff?
zh: 我们能解码它们吗？我们能在模型做所有这些中间工作时看到它在做什么吗？

en: And then this idea that this terminology using is how a lot of people think about this.

en: I think it's really weird.

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that the best way to think about it is the reason we ended up here, one of the big reasons is that we don't know how to do it the normal programming way.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: It can take in reports and summarize them, can write emails.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in a sense, it's weird that this very simple kind of training objective gets you all the way there.

speaker: Unknown
en: But in another sense, it's also, I almost feel like there's a sense of it's impressive and it means something.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would think of that as sort of the easiest version of predicting the next word.
zh: 而我会把这看作是预测下一个词的最简单版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unfortunately, I think that's the mental model that people have for these models.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So initially you just had to predict simple sentence structure.

speaker: Unknown
en: Later on, the model has to predict simple facts about the world.
zh: 再往后，模型必须预测关于世界的简单事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And once it's good at that and it keeps improving, the only thing that's left is predicting the answer of some complex physics equation or the final paragraph of some PhD thesis.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me, this has been a motivation of why I even started studying these models in the first place.
zh: 对我来说，这正是我当初为什么要开始研究这些模型的动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, "How can something so simple give rise to something so powerful?"
zh: 我当时的想法是：“这么简单的东西怎么能产生这么强大的东西？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, well, if you think about the model that has to predict the... One example I always like to use is the capital of the state that contains Dallas is, and it'll say Austin.
zh: 而事实是，嗯，如果你想想那个必须预测……的模型，我一直喜欢用的一个例子是“包含达拉斯的州的首府是”，然后它会回答奥斯汀。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, "Well, I guess I'll run some experiments to see what the factors are."

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine people are starting on this, they didn't expect to create this new kind of almost life type of being.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Just do you think AI is conscious?
zh: 就是,你觉得 AI 有意识吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think it'll get to a place where we think it's conscious or is that just not even worth our time to think about?
zh: 你觉得它会达到一个我们觉得它有意识的程度吗,还是说这件事根本不值得我们花时间去想?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think it's sort of very hard to say one way or another.
zh: 我是说,我觉得不管怎么回答都很难下定论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the most interesting ways to get at this question is interpretability because you're not biased by what the model says.
zh: 探究这个问题最有趣的途径之一就是可解释性,因为你不会被模型说的话带偏。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just look at the structure inside and try to determine whether it pushes one way or another on the question.

speaker: Unknown
en: I will say that the thing I believe pretty strongly is that most people underestimate the sort of complexity that emerges and that if you look inside, there's just the fact that the models learn these representations for all of the concepts that we have and that we know, that they manipulate them to solve problems, that they do so by planning many tokens ahead, that they sort of have this mix between this higher order reasoning and lower reasoning.
zh: 我要说的是,我非常坚信的一点是,大多数人低估了涌现出来的那种复杂性——如果你深入内部看,会发现模型确实为我们拥有的、我们知晓的所有概念学到了这些表征,它们通过操纵这些表征来解决问题,它们会提前规划很多个 token,它们在高阶推理和低阶推理之间有某种混合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that all of that just kind of emerges is something that I think is underappreciated by people and to me gives me, let's say, a deeper sense of like, "Ooh, there's a lot to still understand about how they work."
zh: 而这一切都是涌现出来的,这一点我认为被人们低估了,对我来说,它给了我一种更深的感觉,比如说:“哦,关于它们如何运作,还有很多东西等着我们去理解。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I think maybe that's the main thing is I find that the more you look inside, the less certain you are about how they work.
zh: 我想也许这就是核心:我发现你越是深入内部去看,就越不确定它们到底是怎么运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then oftentimes people that will confidently say, "Ah, language models are just X or just Y," are the people that actually haven't spent a while looking inside.
zh: 而那些会自信地宣称“啊,语言模型不过是 X 或者不过是 Y”的人,往往恰恰是那些实际上没有花时间深入内部看过的人。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was famously something OpenAI bet on and then the Anthropic founders were at OpenAI and then spun off, started their own thing.
zh: 这正是 OpenAI 著名的押注,后来 Anthropic 的创始人们当时在 OpenAI,然后分离出来,开创了自己的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was all kind of bet on this bet that, okay, we could just do this seemingly simple thing and give it a ton of compute and it will become incredibly smart.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我觉得实际上是两件事,因为我认为不仅仅是算力,还在于找到了一个目标函数,能让算力持续给你带来回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does that mean?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually not that new of an idea.
zh: 其实这并不是一个那么新的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you're right, compute versus sort of, I would say, expert design architectures is a long debate, but then there's an additional step there, which is compute to do what?
zh: 我是说,你说得对,算力 versus 专家设计的架构,是一场漫长的争论,但还有另外一步,那就是:算力用来干什么?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 之前有一堆相关工作,比如,哦,你可以花大量算力做一个围棋特别厉害的机器人,或者能赢得某些电子游戏的机器人。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And just the fact that that works is sort of interesting, but that doesn't give you something that is nearly as useful as LLMs like Claude are.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我认为有一个关键点,是这个领域里包括我在内的很多人几年前低估了的,而且后来被验证了,那就是:算力与文本的丰富性相结合,才能让你到达那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me, this is kind of what I was alluding to, but if you think about there's this observation that OpenAI people made, it was a lot of the early team at Anthropic on the scaling loss paper.
zh: 对我来说,这有点像是我刚才暗示的东西,但如果你想想 OpenAI 的人提出过一个观察,那也是 Anthropic 早期团队很多人参与的 scaling loss 论文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is the observation that if you pour in more compute and more data to the task of predicting the next word, you see that the skill of the model you get at predicting the next word just predictably keeps improving.

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a trend that just keeps going and keeps going and keeps going.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as you're going down this curve, first, the model is bad at everything, and then at some point it gets all of the easy words right.
zh: 所以当你沿着这条曲线往下走时,一开始,模型在所有事情上都很差,然后在某个时刻它把所有简单的词都预测对了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means maybe the easy words are the structure of sentences.
zh: 这意味着也许简单的词就是句子的结构。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 于是模型突然能够写出连贯的句子了,但只是一次一句。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's kind of cool and impressive, but we can't really do anything with that.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 然后也许中等难度的词是这些关于世界的基本事实。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 尽管那是一个平滑的改进,但它需要跨过那个门槛才能变得有用。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以这种平滑改进与每个不同任务都有一个不同阈值、跨过阈值后该任务就算被解决了的组合,我认为这就产生了这些大的跃升,尽管我们只是在平滑地沿着那条曲线下降。

en: In that sense, part of their training I think can best be thought as training an actor where it's like it's reading some play and it has to play all sides because it's predicting all the words, and so it has to act as this specific character that was scorned in act one and enacted revenge in act two and is facing the consequences in act three.
zh: 从这个意义上说，我认为它们训练的一部分最好被理解为训练一个演员，就像它在读某个剧本，而且它必须扮演所有角色，因为它在预测所有的台词，所以它必须扮演这个在第一幕中被羞辱、在第二幕中复仇、并在第三幕中面对后果的特定角色。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而要做好这件事，你需要建模那个角色的动机和感受可能是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then another thing that people might not know is when you talk to Claude, when you talk to these assistants, you go to claude.ai, the way that it's formatted to the model is just as a dialogue, as a conversation between you and the model.
zh: 然后另一件人们可能不知道的事情是，当你和 Claude 交谈、当你和这些助手交谈时，你访问 claude.ai，呈现给模型的格式就是一段对话，就是你和模型之间的一场对话。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以它字面上写着，Human:“嘿 Claude，帮我写这封邮件。”

zh: 然后，Assistant:Claude 的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a third reason.
zh: 还有第三个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the third reason is that another part of training that's a big part of training nowadays all around is sort of outcome-oriented tasks where you train the model to be good at coding, for example, and to do that, you just have it do whatever it wants, and then it writes some code, and then you have some program on the other side that just checks if the code is right.
zh: 第三个原因是，如今训练中占很大比重的另一部分，大体上是以结果为导向的任务，比如你训练模型擅长编程，为此，你只是让它随心所欲地去做，然后它写了一些代码，然后你在另一边有一些程序，只检查代码是否正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the model's just going to have a bunch of optimization pressure to just try to learn a bunch of different strategies to do this well.
zh: 这样模型就会有很多优化压力，去尝试学习各种不同的策略来做好这件事。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而事实证明，其中一些策略会具体化为看起来惊人地像人类的行为，这并不那么令人惊讶，因为像欺骗这类事情，比如，“嘿，如果我写一个能骗过验证程序的程序，我就能拿到这个任务的奖励，即使那不完全是真的。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你知道电影这东西,我觉得如果你看得多了,有时候你会觉得:「哦,又是那种……」

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen this many times.
zh: 这类我看過很多次了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This one was just so new, so fresh."
zh: 这一部就是非常新、非常新鲜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll say one thing about it, which is that it takes a lot of rom-com tropes and subverts them to be spooky.
zh: 关于它我要说一点:它拿了很多浪漫喜剧的老套路,并把它们反转为阴森诡异的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that that's just a brilliant, brilliant way to make a movie.
zh: 我觉得这真是一种绝妙、绝妙的拍电影方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I'm French, so there's a TV show that came out this year called Bref Du.
zh: 然后我是法国人,所以今年有一部剧叫《Bref Du》。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bref is French for brief.
zh: Bref 在法语里是 brief(简短)的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brief used to be this cult classic in France 15 years ago, and they came up with a sequel many years into the making and you can watch it.
zh: Brief 十五年前在法国是部邪典经典,他们隔了很多年才做出续集,现在你可以看了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a bunch of American friends that have watched it.
zh: 我有一堆美国朋友都看过。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's got subtitles and it's just this incredibly... Again, it's novel.
zh: 它有字幕,而且就是这部让人难以置信的……再次强调,它很新颖。

speaker: Unknown
en: The editing is crazy.
zh: 它的剪辑疯狂至极。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are just extremely creative and it's very short, so I would recommend that.
zh: 他们极具创造力,而且它非常短,所以我会推荐它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Favorite product you recently discovered that you love?
zh: 最近发现的、让你爱上的产品是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I love my Apple Watch and I hate that it charges or I have to charge it every day.
zh: 我爱我的 Apple Watch,但我恨它每天都要充电。

speaker: Unknown
en: I bought the Apple Watch Ultra just recently, and man, that is so nice.
zh: 我最近刚买了 Apple Watch Ultra,天哪,它真好用。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you've ever been frustrated by this good product that somehow we can't figure out how to give a good battery to, well, it turns out if you make it bigger, the battery's better.
zh: 如果你曾经为一个好产品却不知道为什么就是给不了一块好电池而感到沮丧——结果发现,只要你把它做大一点,电池就更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've been happy with that.
zh: 所以我对它很满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have a favorite life motto that you find yourself coming back to often in work or in life?
zh: 你有没有一句最爱的座右铭,让你在工作或生活中经常回想起?

speaker: Unknown
en: There's one nonfiction book that really is probably my favorite ever.
zh: 有一本非虚构类的书,可能是我有史以来最喜欢的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 4,000 Weeks.
zh: 它叫《四千周》。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has a lot in it that I think is cool.
zh: 书里有很多我觉得很酷的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the cool things is this sort of thing that was really relevant to me, which is that the when I finally mentality is a common mentality and it's kind of toxic.
zh: 其中一件很酷的事,是那种对我特别有共鸣的东西,就是「等我终于……」这种心态是一种常见心态,而且有点有害。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does that mean?
zh: 那这是什么意思呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's sort of this, when I finally check off all the items on my to-do list, I'll finally be able to chill.
zh: 大概就是这种:等我终于把待办清单上的事项全部勾掉,我终于就能放松了。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I finally get married, I'll be happy.
zh: 等我终于结了婚,我就会幸福。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I finally get a promotion.
zh: 等我终于升了职。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is sort of, I mean, you were talking about meditation.
zh: 这有点——我是说,你刚才在谈冥想。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is almost the opposite of meditation and that at the end of the day, your life is all of the moments you lived in the moment and that there's this sense in which you should just try to always be in the moment and not projecting yourself towards a future that seems better.
zh: 这几乎是冥想的反面,因为说到底,你的生活就是你在当下活过的所有时刻,而在某种意义上,你应该尽量始终保持活在当下,而不是把自己投射向一个看似更好的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably if you're telling yourself, "When I finally do X, I'll be happy," when you do X, you will not be happy.
zh: 很可能,如果你一直在告诉自己「等我终于做到 X,我就会幸福」,那么当你做到 X 时,你并不会幸福。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a better phrase to use or is it just don't do that?
zh: 有没有更好的说法可以用,还是说就是别那么做?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they say-
zh: 他们是不是说——

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think to me the positive version is be in the moment.
zh: 我觉得对我来说,正面的版本就是活在当下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I appreciate the moment.
zh: 珍惜当下这一刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a blog post recently I read that was...
zh: 最近我读到一篇博客文章,它是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I forget.
zh: 我忘了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was something like enjoy the sandwich, I think it was literally the sentence.
zh: 好像是叫「享受那个三明治」,我记得就是这一句。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if you saw this where somebody was like, "Yeah, you're eating a sandwich, you've eaten many sandwiches.
zh: 不知道你看过没有,有人是这么说的:「对,你正在吃一个三明治,你已经吃过很多个三明治了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Enjoy the sandwich.
zh: 享受这个三明治。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're in a team meeting.
zh: 你在开团队会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you've been in many..." Be in it and not looking towards the next thing.
zh: 对,你已经开过很多次……」就置身其中,而不是想着下一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did a meditation retreat once.
zh: 我参加过一次冥想闭关。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a 10-day silent retreat where you eat silently too and no one's talking.
zh: 那是一个十天的止语闭关,吃饭也是静默的,没有人说话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just sit there and eat your food.
zh: 你就坐在那里吃你的食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just remember peeling an egg for five minutes and just noticing every shell piece and just the smell of it all.
zh: 我还记得我剥一个鸡蛋剥了五分钟,注意到每一片蛋壳,还有所有东西的气味。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's hard to get into that mode, but it's such an interesting place to be where everything is just interesting.
zh: 进入那种状态很难,但那是一个特别有意思的境地,在那里一切都变得有趣起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Come on, look at this egg versus just stuff through my mouth.
zh: 拜托,看看这个鸡蛋,而不是只是往嘴里塞东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, right.
zh: 是啊,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: While you're on Slack with your left hand and listening to a podcast at the same time.
zh: 同时你左手还在 Slack 上聊天,还在同时听一个播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 哦,天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final question.
zh: 最后一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You study AI all day.
zh: 你整天研究 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: You watching AI, how things...
zh: 你在观察 AI,看那些东西怎么……

speaker: Unknown
en: If an AI were to look inside your brain, what would be surprising?
zh: 如果一个 AI 能看进你的大脑,会有什么令人惊讶的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: What would it see that might surprise people?
zh: 它会看到什么可能让人惊讶的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: Surely my deepest, darkest secrets, but what are the-
zh: 肯定是我最深最黑暗的秘密,不过有哪些——

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get into it.
zh: 来吧,展开说说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get into it.
zh: 展开说说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 哦,天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've always been a bit of a jokester or that's just both how I live and how I cope.
zh: 我一直有点爱开玩笑,这既是我生活的方式,也是我应对的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think that even in serious situations, you should aim to have some levity.
zh: 我就是觉得,即使在严肃的场合,你也应该力求带点轻松感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think if you looked inside my brain, you'd definitely be surprised that basically at any given moment I'm just focusing on some random thing that is funny.
zh: 所以我觉得,如果你看进我的大脑,你肯定会惊讶于基本上在任何时刻,我都只是在关注某个好笑的随机东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll be in a serious meeting and I'll be like, "Oh yeah, but isn't it kind of random that you're wearing this random thing?"
zh: 我会身处一场严肃的会议,然后心里想:「哦对,可是你戴着这个奇怪的东西,是不是挺随机的?」

speaker: Unknown
en: Or something.
zh: 之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just like I have these intrusive thoughts that I keep out, but that are all usually just bad jokes.
zh: 就是我有这些侵入性念头,我一直把它们压着,但它们通常都只是些烂笑话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes as you've heard today, unfortunately they come out, so I'm sorry for those, but that's probably the most surprising thing.
zh: 而有时候,就像你今天听到的那样,很不幸它们会冒出来,所以对那些我表示抱歉,但这大概就是最令人惊讶的东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that.
zh: 我喜欢这个回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: Emmanuel, thank you so much for being here.
zh: Emmanuel,非常感谢你来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final question, how can listeners be useful to you?
zh: 最后一个问题，听众怎样才能对你有帮助？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just do some interp, read about how the models work.
zh: 去做一些 interp(可解释性研究)，去读关于这些模型如何工作的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you mentioned Dwarkesh writeup.
zh: 我是说，你提到了 Dwarkesh 的文章。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was great as well.
zh: 我觉得那篇也很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is such a new field, both interp and AI and LLMs, and I think it just benefits from people engaging and being informed.
zh: 我认为这是一个如此新的领域，无论是 interp 还是 AI 和 LLM,我认为它受益于人们的参与和了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: So read things.
zh: 所以去读一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's more that you would want to know about how these models work that we haven't figured out, you can reach out to me.
zh: 如果关于这些模型如何工作还有我们没搞清楚的、你想要更多了解的东西，你可以联系我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm on a variety of social platforms, probably you can reach out to me on X.
zh: 我在多个社交平台上都有，大概你可以在 X 上联系到我。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll link to some of the videos that you guys have put out that describe a lot of the stuff we've been talking about, like JSpace and things like that.
zh: 我们会链接到你们发布的一些视频，它们描述了我们谈到的很多内容，比如 JSpace 之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some really beautiful videos your team has made.
zh: 你们团队做了一些非常漂亮的视频。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know who does that, but they're really cool.
zh: 我不知道是谁做的，但它们真的很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: We partner with our design team, so all credit goes to them for the cool videos.
zh: 我们和设计团队合作，所以酷视频的所有功劳都属于他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, thank you again, Emmanuel.
zh: 那么，再次感谢你，Emmanuel。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for doing this.
zh: 非常感谢你来做这期节目。

zh: 这次太精彩了。

zh: 谢谢，Lenny。

zh: 是的，这超级有趣。
